clinical.quoteLong: It was on me after a hike and I got the whole thing out with tweezers — head and all, I checked twice. No rash, I feel fine, but the internet was very dramatic about it.
clinical.presentationShort: 31yo F — engorged tick removed intact 6h ago after a hike. No rash, no fever, no systemic symptoms.
clinical.presentationLong: 31-year-old female who removed an intact tick six hours after a hike, with no rash, fever or systemic symptoms.

diagnosis.primary: Uncomplicated tick bite, tick removed intact
diagnosis.esi2roomsNotes: ESI 5: no ED treatment-area resources are expected; brief evaluation, counseling, and discharge are appropriate.
diagnosis.disposition: Discharge → wound care and clear advice to return for an expanding rash or fever over the next 30 days
diagnosis.why: Removed intact, no rash, no fever, and well inside the transmission window. Nothing to do here but educate and set return precautions.

aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character. Match the painterly STYLE of the attached reference image - its brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting and palette - but do NOT copy its cropping, camera distance or composition. FRAMING (follow exactly): a full-body WIDE SHOT, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, subject centred. The ENTIRE figure must be inside the frame from the top of the head to the soles of both feet, and the ENTIRE chair must be inside the frame including all four chair legs meeting the floor. Leave clear empty margin on all four sides - roughly 10% of the image width as space above the head and below the feet. This is NOT a close-up, NOT a bust, NOT a head-and-shoulders portrait, NOT a cropped view: the camera is pulled well back so the whole person and the whole chair sit comfortably inside the picture with room around them. Draw the COMPLETE body - head, neck, torso, both arms, both hands, lap, both legs, both feet with shoes. Nothing cropped by the edges, no missing or truncated limbs, no body part fading out or left unfinished. Subject: a white 31-year-old woman in hiking clothes with a small plaster on her forearm, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: sitting relaxed with one sleeve rolled up, showing her forearm. Expression: calm and slightly apologetic for coming in. Clearly visible: a small plaster on the forearm; hiking clothes and boots. Overall: entirely well.
